job.title: Chief Transformation Officer - ANROWS
job.description:
• Partner with the CEO and Executive Leadership Team to lead enterprise-wide transformation and embed ANROWS’ strategic priorities through effective planning, systems, governance and delivery.
  • Strengthen leadership capability, collaboration, trust, accountability and sustainable ways of working following ANROWS’ recent transformation and restructure.
  • Establish the structures, processes and cross-functional arrangements that enable ANROWS’ specialist directorates to deliver its strategy effectively, with clear responsibilities, decision-making authority and measures of success.

Lead enterprise-wide transformation at ANROWS, partnering with the CEO to strengthen culture, systems, governance and organisational effectiveness.

About ANROWS

ANROWS is Australia's independent source for evidence on domestic, family, sexual and gender-based violence.

The organisation is entering an important phase of development as it embeds its strategic priorities and strengthens the organisational foundations required to deliver them effectively. This includes improving organisational clarity, integration, accountability and sustainable performance.

The opportunity

Reporting to the Chief Executive Officer, the Chief Transformation Officer will partner with the CEO and Executive Leadership Team to lead ANROWS’ enterprise-wide transformation agenda, translating strategic priorities into practical organisational planning, governance, systems, decision-making and delivery. This is an organisation-wide role, focused on creating clarity across the organisation while ensuring leadership retains accountability for their specialist portfolios.

ANROWS’ specialist directorates include Research and Insights, Knowledge Exchange and Engagement, Strategic Communications, Finance and Operations and People and Culture, with responsibilities spanning research and evaluation, evidence mobilisation and stakeholder engagement, communications and reputation, financial and operational management, and organisational capability. The CTO will connect these functions through clearer responsibilities, decision-making authority, shared accountability and effective ways of working, without duplicating the responsibilities of the respective directors.

Your impact

Working closely with the CEO and Executive Leadership Team, you will translate ANROWS' strategic priorities into clear organisational plans, delivery rhythms and measures of success. You will strengthen enterprise-wide planning, governance, reporting, systems and decision-making, while clarifying responsibilities and accountabilities across the organisation.

You will support the Leadership Team to operate with greater collaboration, enterprise-wide thinking and shared accountability. You will also help strengthen trust, confidence, reflection, feedback and sustainable ways of working across ANROWS, working closely with People and Culture and the broader leadership team with a key focus on establishing the cross-functional arrangements that allow ANROWS' specialist directorates to work together effectively.

What does success look like?

Success will be measured by your ability to turn ANROWS' strategic priorities into practical organisational planning, systems, governance and delivery practices. You will create greater clarity around how priorities are set, decisions are made, responsibilities are held and progress is measured.

Within 12 to 24 months, you will have strengthened enterprise-wide leadership, built greater trust and confidence across the organisation and established more integrated ways of working across ANROWS' specialist functions. Directors will retain accountability for their areas while working within clearer interfaces, shared priorities and decision-making arrangements.

By the end of the appointment, ANROWS will have stronger organisational capability, more effective systems and routines, improved collaboration and clearer accountability, with the changes sufficiently embedded to continue beyond the tenure of the role.

About you

You are an experienced enterprise leader who has delivered complex organisational transformation beyond strategy development and into practical implementation. You will bring experience strengthening leadership capability, culture, collaboration, accountability, organisational planning, governance, systems and ways of working. Your background may include enterprise transformation, organisational development, strategy and operations, corporate services, Chief Operating Officer, Chief of Staff or broad executive leadership. Experience in a purpose-driven, stakeholder-rich or independent organisation will be highly relevant.

Direct experience in domestic, family, sexual or gender-based violence, research or government is valuable but not essential. What matters most is your ability to connect strategy, people, culture, systems, governance and delivery while respecting the expertise and accountability of specialist leaders.

job.title: General Manager, Investment - BEDA
job.description:
• Lead Brisbane’s investment agenda and shape the city’s future economic growth
  • Influence major investment decisions and unlock opportunities for our city
  • Join a high-performing executive team at a defining moment for Brisbane’s future

This is Brisbane’s Decade

Brisbane is entering a defining decade. New infrastructure, industries and precincts are reshaping our economy, while Brisbane 2032 is bringing global attention and opportunity to our city.

At Brisbane Economic Development Agency (BEDA), we’re looking for a General Manager, Investment to help turn that momentum into lasting economic outcomes, strengthen Brisbane's competitive position and make a compelling case for our city to investors, businesses and talent across the world.

This is more than managing an investment attraction team. It’s an opportunity to see potential before it becomes obvious, understand how cities compete for investment, talent and ideas, and bring people together to turn opportunity into action.

What you’ll lead

As a key member of BEDA’s Executive Leadership Team, reporting to the CEO, you’ll lead the Investment function across investment attraction, business expansion and reinvestment, infrastructure investment and economic intelligence.

You’ll be accountable for the opportunities BEDA pursues, the relationships it builds and the economic outcomes it creates. Working with government, industry and investors, you’ll help Brisbane attract investment and businesses that create jobs, build capability and strengthen the city’s priority industries.

Who we’re looking for

We’re less interested in where you’ve worked than what you’ve led, built and delivered. Your background may be in economics, finance, investment, banking, infrastructure, property, economic development, government, professional services or industry.

What matters is a strong track record of results, commercial and economic acumen, strategic judgement and the ability to turn complex opportunities into action. You’ll have proven experience leading high-performing teams, developing talented people and creating the clarity and accountability they to succeed.

You’ll be comfortable interrogating the numbers, challenging assumptions and making difficult decisions - whether in a boardroom, a Minister’s office, an international investor meeting or with Brisbane’s business leaders. Just as importantly, you’ll build trusted relationships, influence at senior levels and tell a compelling economic story.

Above all, you’ll bring curiosity, ambition and a genuine belief in Brisbane’s potential.

Why BEDA?

We believe economic development is so much more than reports, transactions and targets. It's about creating possibility: a company choosing Brisbane, a local business expanding, an investor backing an idea, a new industry taking root and people accessing opportunities that didn't exist before.

That's the privilege of working at BEDA. You'll join a passionate, collaborative organisation where ideas are encouraged, leadership is empowered and the opportunity to make a difference is real. Few cities offer the canvas Brisbane does right now.

Help shape what’s next

We’re looking for a leader who will challenge our thinking, ask the difficult questions and help BEDA, its partners and Brisbane achieve more.

If you can see the opportunity ahead and have the ambition to turn it into reality, we’d like to hear from you.

Come and help build what’s next for Brisbane.

job.title: Safety Advisor
job.description:
• Lead practical safety across capital works, operations and contractor-delivered projects.
  • Help protect people and communities while strengthening a proactive safety culture.

The opportunity

Davidson is partnering with a large, complex organisation that delivers essential services to the community to appoint a Safety Advisor.

Reporting to the Group Manager, Safety & Wellbeing, you will provide practical safety leadership across the full project lifecycle, from design and mobilisation through to delivery, commissioning and handover.

Working closely with engineers, project managers, operational leaders, contractors and frontline employees, you will identify and manage risks, strengthen safety capability and support effective controls across project and operational environments.

This opportunity will suit an established Safety Advisor who can quickly understand a complex operating environment, build trusted relationships and provide credible, practical advice from the outset.

Your responsibilities

  • Provide safety advice to leaders, employees, project teams and contractors.
  • Support capital projects and operational teams throughout the project lifecycle.
  • Conduct risk assessments, workplace inspections, audits, safety observations and control-effectiveness reviews.
  • Support the identification and management of critical risks and site safety risk registers.
  • Lead or contribute to incident investigations, including ICAM investigations where required.
  • Work with contractors and delivery partners to promote consistent safety standards and accountability.
  • Deliver safety training, inductions and toolbox talks.
  • Coach leaders and employees in risk management and safe work practices.
  • Monitor safety performance, identify trends and recommend practical improvements.
  • Contribute to the continued development of the safety management system and proactive safety culture.

About you

You will bring experience as a Safety Advisor in a complex, high-risk or operational environment. Your background may include utilities, civil construction, infrastructure, engineering, transport, energy or another project-based industry.

You will ideally have:

  • Tertiary qualifications in Work Health and Safety, Occupational Health, Risk Management or a related discipline.
  • Strong knowledge of OHS/WHS legislation, regulations and relevant standards.
  • Experience in hazard identification, risk assessment and critical-control management.
  • Experience across audits, assurance, compliance and safety systems.
  • Experience with incident investigations and ICAM methodology.
  • The ability to translate technical and legislative requirements into practical solutions.
  • Strong stakeholder engagement, influencing and communication skills.
  • A collaborative and practical approach to safety leadership.
  • Sound judgement, resilience and the ability to manage competing priorities.
  • A current driver’s licence and the ability to travel to operational and delivery-partner sites.

Experience in psychosocial risk, employee wellbeing and broader safety culture initiatives will be viewed favourably. Strong technical, project and operational safety experience is the primary requirement.

Working environment

This is a visible and hands-on role involving engagement across capital project and operational sites, including active construction and live operational environments. Personal protective equipment will be required when visiting relevant sites.

The role is expected to involve approximately three days per week in the office, with travel to operational and delivery-partner sites as required. You will also participate in an after-hours standby roster and provide emergency response and incident support when required.

Flexible working arrangements are available, including the potential for compressed hours or a nine-day fortnight, subject to operational requirements.


Why join?

This is an opportunity to join an organisation delivering essential services to the community and contribute to practical improvements that protect people, support reliable operations and strengthen safety outcomes.

You will enjoy broad exposure across projects and operations, the opportunity to work with diverse stakeholders and the ability to make a genuine contribution to safety culture and maturity.

job.title: Site Manager – Renewable Energy Infrastructure
job.description:
About the Company

Iberdrola Australia is part of the global Iberdrola Group, a leading renewable energy company committed to accelerating the transition to a cleaner, more sustainable energy future. With a growing portfolio of renewable energy generation and storage assets across Australia, Iberdrola continues to invest in critical infrastructure that supports the nation's evolving energy needs.

As part of this investment, Iberdrola is delivering a major Battery Energy Storage System (BESS) project at Tungkillo, approximately one hour from Adelaide. With construction underway, this project presents an exciting opportunity to contribute to the delivery of significant energy infrastructure in South Australia.

About the Role

Davidson is partnering with Iberdrola Australia to recruit an experienced Site Manager to provide client-side leadership and oversight of construction activities at its Tungkillo BESS project.

Reporting to the Project Manager, you will act as Iberdrola's representative on site, overseeing contractor performance, coordinating construction activities and ensuring works are delivered safely, efficiently and in accordance with project requirements.

A key focus will be the delivery of high-voltage electrical infrastructure, particularly substation works, alongside the management of multidisciplinary contractors and site interfaces.

Beyond construction oversight, you will play an important role in maintaining positive relationships with local councils, community representatives, landowners and other key stakeholders, ensuring effective communication throughout the project lifecycle.

Key responsibilities will include:

  • Overseeing daily site activities, with a focus on safety, quality, construction progress and contractor performance.
  • Managing interfaces across civil, electrical and high-voltage infrastructure works, ensuring effective coordination between contractors and project teams.
  • Monitoring construction programmes, identifying delivery risks and escalating issues to maintain project momentum.
  • Championing a strong safety culture and ensuring compliance with HSE standards and project requirements.
  • Building and maintaining effective relationships with local councils, community stakeholders, landowners and external consultants.
  • Supporting project reporting, quality assurance, construction handovers and the transition into commissioning and project close-out.

About You

You are an accomplished Site Manager or senior construction professional with a proven track record delivering complex electrical infrastructure, major construction or renewable energy projects.

You bring strong technical understanding, sound commercial judgement and the confidence to represent a project owner while managing experienced principal contractors and diverse stakeholder groups.

To be successful, you will demonstrate:

  • Significant site management or senior construction supervision experience across major infrastructure, high-voltage electrical, substation or renewable energy projects.
  • Strong knowledge of HV infrastructure, ideally including 275kV or 330kV substation environments.
  • Proven experience managing principal contractors, coordinating multidisciplinary site teams and maintaining construction delivery standards.
  • Strong HSE leadership, with the ability to proactively identify risks, resolve issues and drive accountability.
  • Excellent stakeholder engagement and communication skills, particularly when working with local communities, councils and external parties.
  • The ability to interpret engineering drawings, manage construction priorities and contribute to effective project planning and reporting.

Previous experience on utility-scale BESS, solar or wind farm projects will be highly regarded, although candidates with a strong background in high-voltage substations or transmission infrastructure are equally encouraged to apply.

Experience working with South Australian network service providers, including Enerven, would be advantageous.

The Benefits

This is an opportunity to join a globally recognised renewable energy business and play a pivotal role in delivering critical energy infrastructure in South Australia.

  • Permanent career opportunity: Join Iberdrola Australia with the potential to contribute to future projects beyond the Tungkillo development.
  • Major project exposure: Take ownership of site delivery activities on a significant battery storage development, with commercial operation targeted for May 2028.
  • Competitive remuneration: An attractive salary package with short-term incentive opportunities.
  • Lifestyle and location: Work approximately one hour from Adelaide, with accommodation provided close to site during rostered working periods.
  • Work-life balance: A structured site roster with standard working hours, rather than extended 12-hour construction shifts.

If you are an experienced Site Manager with a strong background in high-voltage infrastructure and are looking to make a meaningful contribution to Australia's renewable energy future, we encourage you to apply.

  • Configured and tested alert rules, thresholds, severity, routing and evidence views.
  • Documented tuning decisions, known limitations, operational runbooks and Confluence knowledge articles.
  • Knowledge-transfer sessions and handover documentation for application, security and platform support teams.

  • Hands-on experience with Kibana dashboards, Lens, filters, controls, drill-downs, saved searches and dashboard usability.
  • Practical knowledge of Elasticsearch and ELK concepts, including indices, data views, fields, aggregations and query performance.
  • Strong KQL skills for investigation, monitoring and alerting use cases.

  • Ability to analyse application logs to identify operational failures, security-relevant events, patterns and root causes.
  • Experience with Java application logs, stack traces, logging frameworks and application behaviour.
  • DevOps experience, including Linux/Unix, shell scripting, CI/CD awareness, release support, environment validation and automation activities.
  • Experience using Jira and Confluence to manage delivery and maintain operational knowledge.
  • Strong troubleshooting, written communication, stakeholder engagement and handover skills

Desirable Skills and Experience:

  • Experience with Elastic alerting, rule management, connectors and case or incident workflow integration.
  • Exposure to Azure Monitor, Microsoft Sentinel, CI/CD tooling, cloud platforms or other SIEM and security operations platforms.
  • Understanding of secure logging practices, monitoring control assurance and operational support models.

job.description:
The opportunity

Davidson is partnering with a large, privately owned multinational business to appoint a Head of Financial Control – APAC.

Based on the Gold Coast and reporting to the APAC CFO, this is a broad finance leadership role with responsibility for financial control, reporting, governance and performance across the region.

You will lead an established finance team and work closely with senior leaders across Finance, Operations, Sales and the wider business.

The brief is clear. They need someone who can keep the fundamentals tight, improve how the function operates and give the CFO confidence in the numbers, controls and team.

You will ideally bring:

  • CA or CPA qualification
  • Senior financial control experience
  • Experience in manufacturing, FMCG, distribution or another inventory-based environment
  • Strong statutory and management reporting capability
  • Sound knowledge of Australian tax, treasury, governance and compliance
  • Experience with inventory, costing and working capital
  • Strong budgeting, forecasting and FP&A capability
  • Experience with large ERP systems and finance transformation
  • Proven experience leading and developing a finance team

You will need to be comfortable getting into the detail when required, but also able to step back, understand what is happening across the business and give clear advice to senior leaders.

The attraction is the breadth.

For someone who enjoys building stronger finance functions and helping teams perform better, this is a meaningful leadership opportunity.

JOB TITLE: Workday Integration Support Lead

JOB LOCATION: Melbourne preferred; Sydney and Adelaide candidates also considered (Hybrid)

Role Overview

We are seeking an experienced Workday Integration Support Lead to own the operational stability, support, governance, and continuous improvement of integrations between Workday and enterprise platforms. The role will lead L2/L3 integration support, coordinate incident resolution, manage monitoring and release activities, and provide technical leadership across inbound and outbound interfaces. The successful candidate will work closely with Workday functional teams, security, reporting, infrastructure, middleware, third-party vendors, and business stakeholders to ensure integrations remain reliable, secure, supportable, and aligned with business priorities.

Key Responsibilities

Integration Support Leadership

  • Lead day-to-day L2/L3 production support for Workday integrations, interfaces, and scheduled data transfers.
  • Act as the technical escalation point for high-priority incidents, recurring failures, and complex integration defects.
  • Triage incidents, determine business impact, coordinate resolver teams, and drive issues through to root-cause resolution.
  • Prioritise break-fix, service requests, minor enhancements, regulatory changes, and technical debt within the support backlog.
  • Coordinate with Workday functional leads to assess business-process, security, reporting, and configuration dependencies.
  • Provide clear stakeholder updates during incidents and escalate risks, constraints, and vendor dependencies when required.

Monitoring and Operational Control

  • Own integration monitoring, alerting, daily health checks, failure management, restart procedures, and operational dashboards.
  • Monitor scheduled and event-driven integrations, including inbound, outbound, file-based, API-based, and middleware-managed interfaces.
  • Ensure failures are identified promptly, data is reprocessed safely, and downstream impacts are assessed before closure.
  • Define support thresholds, alert routing, on-call or after-hours escalation requirements, and operational hand-offs.
  • Maintain integration inventories, schedules, dependencies, owners, service criticality, and support contacts.
  • Track availability, incident trends, repeat failures, ageing defects, and service performance for governance reporting.

Technical Troubleshooting and Development

  • Troubleshoot Workday integrations using integration event details, process monitor, audit information, reports, logs, and error outputs.
  • Support and enhance integrations built with Workday Studio, Enterprise Interface Builder (EIB), Core Connectors, Cloud Connect, Report-as-a-Service (RaaS), Workday Web Services, REST/SOAP APIs, and custom reports.
  • Analyse and resolve issues involving XSLT, XML, JSON, CSV, web services, authentication, certificates, encryption, file transfer, data transformation, and sequencing.
  • Coordinate troubleshooting across middleware and external platforms, including SFTP endpoints, banking, payroll, procurement, asset-management, billing, HR, and identity systems.
  • Build or modify integration components where appropriate, following design, security, testing, and change-control standards.
  • Perform impact analysis before changes to Workday business processes, security, calculated fields, reports, endpoints, or external-system specifications.

Release, Change and Environment Management

  • Lead technical assessment and regression planning for Workday feature releases and integration-impacting changes.
  • Manage integration changes through development, test, deployment, and post-production validation in line with change-management controls.
  • Coordinate tenant refresh impacts, endpoint updates, credentials, certificates, schedules, and post-refresh validation.
  • Prepare deployment plans, backout plans, verification steps, implementation evidence, and change records.
  • Support cutover, go-live, hypercare, and transition-to-support activities for new projects and interfaces.
  • Ensure separation of duties and appropriate approvals are maintained across build, migration, and production support.

Security, Compliance and Risk

  • Partner with Workday Security teams to maintain integration system users, integration security groups, domain permissions, authentication methods, and least-privilege access.
  • Monitor certificate, key, password, token, and endpoint expiry risks and coordinate timely renewals.
  • Ensure sensitive data is appropriately protected in transit and at rest, including secure file transfer, encryption, masking, and controlled logging.
  • Support audit requests by providing configuration, access, change, test, and operational evidence.
  • Maintain integration risks, known errors, control gaps, remediation actions, and continuity procedures.

Governance, Documentation and Continuous Improvement

  • Chair or contribute to integration support reviews, incident reviews, change forums, release planning, and service-governance meetings.
  • Own or maintain integration design documents, support guides, runbooks, monitoring procedures, data mappings, interface catalogues, and knowledge articles.
  • Conduct root-cause analysis for significant or recurring incidents and ensure preventative actions are implemented.
  • Identify opportunities to reduce manual intervention, improve observability, standardise patterns, and retire fragile interfaces.
  • Provide coaching, work allocation, technical review, and knowledge transfer for integration support consultants and partner resources.
  • Collaborate with implementation partners and vendors while retaining clear internal ownership of service outcomes.

Required Skills & Qualifications

  • 7+ years of Workday integration experience, including significant experience in production support or managed-service environments.
  • Hands-on expertise with Workday Studio, EIB, Core Connectors, RaaS, custom reports, calculated fields, Workday Web Services, and REST/SOAP APIs.
  • Strong troubleshooting capability across XML, XSLT, JSON, web services, SFTP, PGP encryption, certificates, authentication, and data transformation.
  • Experience leading incident, problem, change, and release activities for business-critical integrations.
  • Working knowledge of Workday security concepts relevant to integrations, including integration system users, security groups, domains, and least-privilege access.
  • Experience with integration monitoring, operational dashboards, service reporting, root-cause analysis, and support documentation.
  • Ability to coordinate technical and functional teams, external vendors, and business stakeholders during high-impact incidents.
  • Strong written and verbal communication, prioritisation, documentation, and stakeholder-management skills.
  • Availability to support Australian business hours and planned after-hours releases or critical incidents when required.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Workday integration certification or relevant Workday Pro accreditation.
  • Experience with middleware or integration platforms such as MuleSoft, Boomi, Azure Integration Services, or similar enterprise tools.
  • Experience supporting integrations across Workday Financials, Procurement, Strategic Sourcing, Payroll, HCM, Banking, and enterprise asset-management platforms.
  • Knowledge of ITIL-based incident, problem, change, request, and service-level management practices.
  • Experience in utilities, regulated industries, multi-company environments, or complex enterprise application landscapes.
  • Experience with ticketing and engineering tools such as ServiceNow, Jira, or Azure DevOps.
  • Understanding of privacy, records management, audit, and cyber-security control requirements.

Success Measures

  • Stable and reliable operation of critical Workday integrations.
  • Timely incident resolution and effective stakeholder communication.
  • Reduction in repeat failures through root-cause elimination and preventative improvements.
  • Controlled and auditable releases with successful post-deployment validation.
  • Accurate support documentation, integration inventory, and operational ownership.
  • Effective knowledge transfer and improved capability across the support team.

Why Join

  • Collaborate with business and technology stakeholders across complex cloud and third-party environments.

About the Company

We are seeking a Cyber Security Architect to play a pivotal role in shaping and protecting the technology environment that supports Barwon Water's customers, community and critical infrastructure. This is an opportunity to influence security strategy across enterprise IT, Operational Technology (OT), Internet of Things (IoT), cloud platforms and emerging technologies

About the Role

Reporting to the Cyber Security Lead, you will be responsible for defining and guiding Barwon Water's security architecture, ensuring security is embedded into technology solutions by design. Working closely with business architects, delivery teams, vendors, engineers and technology stakeholders, you will provide expert advice on the controls, standards and patterns required to deliver secure and resilient solutions.

You will also help shape the organisation's cyber monitoring and incident response capabilities, providing technical leadership across IT, OT and IoT environments and contributing to architecture governance and risk management activities.

Key responsibilities:

  • Define and maintain cyber security architecture standards, patterns and secure-by-design principles across enterprise, cloud, OT and IoT environments.
  • Lead security reviews and provide architectural guidance for projects, technology investments and third-party solutions.
  • Ensure appropriate security controls, monitoring, logging and detection capabilities are embedded across Barwon Water's technology landscape.
  • Provide technical leadership during cyber security incidents, supporting investigation, response, recovery and continuous improvement activities.
  • Identify, assess and manage cyber security risks, ensuring compliance with relevant frameworks, standards and regulatory requirements.
  • Collaborate with architects, engineers, project teams and business stakeholders to deliver secure, resilient and scalable technology solutions.
  • Contribute to architecture governance, technology roadmaps and strategic initiatives that strengthen organisational security maturity.
  • Evaluate emerging technologies, including AI-driven security capabilities and automation, while assessing associated cyber security risks and opportunities.

About You

You are a security professional with a passion for architecture, governance and securing critical infrastructure environments. You bring strong technical expertise and can confidently engage with both technical and business stakeholders.

You will ideally have:

  • Experience in cyber security, security architecture or enterprise technology.
  • Exposure to IT, cloud, OT and/or IoT environments.
  • Knowledge of security frameworks including NIST CSF, ASD Essential Eight, SOCI and IEC 62443.
  • Strong understanding of identity, access management and security control design.
  • Experience participating in architecture governance and design review forums.
  • Excellent stakeholder engagement and communication skills.
  • A continuous improvement mindset and interest in emerging technologies, including AI-driven security solutions.


The Benefits

  • Permanent position with ability to take full ownership
  • Hybrid and flexible working arrangements
  • Collaborative and supportive culture

job.title: Operational Technology Engineer
job.description:
About the Company

Iberdrola Australia is leading Australia’s transition to a clean energy future. With over 125 years history, the Iberdrola Group today is a global energy leader. Their expertise includes renewable energy, networks, smart grids, large-scale energy storage, energy innovation and digitisation, and advanced customer products.

Their generation portfolio is more than 95% renewable and includes 10 wind farms, 3 solar farms, 4 grid scale batteries and 2 fast-start peakers and continuing to evolve, investing in new capabilities in networks and offshore wind. Iberdrola’s financial strength, supply chain access and history of award-winning expertise, will make Iberdrola a certain partner to accelerate Australia’s Net Zero emissions future.

Iberdrola is now recruiting for an experienced OT Engineer to provide technical leadership and coordination of SCADA, control systems and OT project scopes, predominantly for new assets.

This is an opportunity to shape your career with one of the genuine global energy leaders within Australia.


About the Role

Reporting to the Senior OT Manager, and based in either the Sydney or Brisbane CBD office, this role is responsible for ensuring OT and SCADA solutions meet project, operational and compliance requirements from design through commissioning, coordinating interfaces between work packages, managing technical risks, and supporting successful project delivery.

It will act as the primary technical point of contact for OT related project activities, working closely with contractors, vendors and internal stakeholders to review designs and documentation, coordinate testing and acceptance activities, and support project delivery. The role also contributes to the support and continuous improvement of operational OT and SCADA systems, including troubleshooting, lifecycle activities and the delivery of minor enhancement projects.


About You

To be successful in this role you will have tertiary qualifications in electrical engineering, or related discipline, and demonstrated experience in control, SCADA and OT systems within the renewable energy sector or comparable industrial environment.

The ability to balance technical detail with project delivery objectives and to make sound engineering decisions in a multi-disciplinary environment, will be necessary for this role.

Your excellent interpersonal skills allow you to build effective working relationships with colleagues and stakeholders, resulting in exceptional performance.


The Benefits

This is an exceptional career opportunity to join a world leader in renewable energy and contribute to renewable energy projects across Australia.
